facts.text: A job site is any place where heavy machines work; the booklet focuses on surface mines, underground mines, quarries and construction sites.
facts.quote: A job site is any place where heavy machines work, and the booklet is concerned with four main kinds: surface mines, underground mines, quarries and construction sites.

facts.text: Surface mines are stepped open pits where material is dug at the bottom, carried up ramps by haul trucks along haul roads, and dumped on waste piles or taken to a plant.
facts.quote: A *surface mine* (open pit) is a huge stepped hole. Material is dug at the bottom, carried up ramps by haul trucks along haul roads, and dumped on waste piles or taken to a plant.

facts.text: Loaded trucks at surface mines can reach 40 to 50 km/h.
facts.quote: Loaded trucks can reach 40 to 50 km/h

facts.text: The worst surface-mine accidents include trucks running over light vehicles, going through edge barriers and reversing over dump edges.
facts.quote: the worst accidents are trucks running over light vehicles, trucks going through edge barriers, and trucks reversing over dump edges

facts.text: Underground mines have confined tunnel roadways, low and long machines, lower speeds, and workers often on foot close to machines.
facts.quote: An *underground mine* is a network of tunnels. Machines are low and long, speeds are lower, roadways are confined, and workers are often on foot close to machines.

facts.text: The booklet's underground-mine evidence concerns continuous mining machines, shuttle cars and load-haul-dump machines (LHDs) striking or pinning people.
facts.quote: The booklet's underground evidence concerns continuous mining machines, shuttle cars and LHDs striking or pinning people

facts.text: Quarries produce stone, sand and gravel and contain rock faces, crushers, stockpiles and loading areas, usually with smaller trucks and loaders.
facts.quote: A *quarry* produces stone, sand and gravel, with a rock face, crushers, stockpiles and loading areas, usually with smaller trucks and loaders.

facts.text: British guidance says transport accounts for 40% of quarry accidents and 60% of quarry deaths.
facts.quote: British guidance says transport accounts for 40% of quarry accidents and 60% of quarry deaths

facts.text: Reversing over people is described as the classic quarry accident.
facts.quote: reversing over people is the classic quarry accident

facts.text: Construction sites mix machines with public traffic, delivery trucks and many workers on foot in confined space.
facts.quote: A *construction site* mixes machines with public traffic, delivery trucks and many workers on foot in confined space.

facts.text: At US road construction sites, being struck by a vehicle or machine was the most common cause of death from 2005 to 2016.
facts.quote: At US road construction sites, being struck by a vehicle or machine was the most common cause of death from 2005 to 2016

facts.text: The challenge statement says one machine type may work across 100 or more job sites and applications.
facts.quote: The challenge statement says one machine type may work across 100 or more job sites and applications [Introduction].

facts.text: For simulation, the booklet translates job-site and application diversity into operating-domain parameters: site type (pit, quarry face, stockpile yard, road works, building site, forest, field), surface (gravel, mud, snow, ice, paved), slope, object classes, weather and light, machine model and sensor pose.
facts.quote: operating-domain parameters: site type (pit, quarry face, stockpile yard, road works, building site, forest, field), surface (gravel, mud, snow, ice, paved), slope, object classes, weather and light, machine model and sensor pose [Chapter 5].

facts.text: The same braking algorithm gives different safety results at sites with different traffic separation, intersection rules and pedestrian controls, making site type a main dimension the virtual validation program must cover.
facts.quote: The same braking algorithm gives different safety results at sites with different traffic separation, intersection rules and pedestrian controls, so site type is a main dimension the virtual program must cover [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The booklet concludes that no single method can produce valid virtual environments for all site types in the time available.
facts.quote: The booklet concludes that no single method can produce valid virtual environments for all site types in the time available

facts.text: The booklet recommends a library of parameterized representative site types anchored to a few surveyed real sites as the realistic route to virtual environments.
facts.quote: a library of parameterized representative site types anchored to a few surveyed real sites is the realistic route [Chapter 5].
